'''Damion Marquez Williams James''' (born October 7, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He played college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]].

==High school career==
Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], James was listed as the No. 7 small forward and the No. 17 player in the nation in 2006.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Damion-James-25393;_ylt=AvWkIcIm6kXlKWBT00BMPJrXO5B4 Damion James Recruiting Profile]</ref> He initially signed to play college basketball at the [[University of Oklahoma]] for head coach [[Kelvin Sampson]]. When Sampson took the head coaching position at [[Indiana University]], the administration at Oklahoma released James from his letter of intent and he switched his decision to Texas.

==College career==

===Freshman season===
James started all 35 games, along with fellow freshmen [[Kevin Durant]] and [[D. J. Augustin]], in leading the Longhorns to a 25–10 record. James averaged 25.9 minutes per contest, with 7.6 points and 7.2 rebounds.<ref name=stats>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/damion-james-1.html Damion James Stats] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221220706/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/damion-james-1.html |date=February 21, 2014 }}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
James averaged 13.2 points and 10.3 rebounds,<ref name="stats" /> helping Texas win a share of the Big 12 regular season title. While talking about the Texas Longhorns on Selection Sunday, Dick Vitale said that James may be the most athletic player in all of college basketball. He also shot 43.6% from behind the arc.

===Junior season===
James, along with [[A. J. Abrams]] and Justin Mason, started all 35 games for the Texas Longhorns that went 23–12 and advanced to the second round of the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. He averaged 15.4 points and 9.2 rebounds with double doubles in 16 of the games on his way to earning a spot on the All-Big 12 Conference Second Team.<ref name="stats" /> On April 15, 2009, James entered his name into the [[2009 NBA draft]], without hiring an agent, and thus retaining his NCAA eligibility.<ref>[http://www.texassports.com/news/2009/4/15/041509aaa_345.aspx James to declare for NBA Draft]</ref> On June 13, 2009, it was reported that James pulled his name from the draft after not being guaranteed a first-round draft position.

===Senior season===
As a senior, James averaged 18.0 points, 10.3 rebounds, and one assist per game.<ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==
James was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 24th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] for the rights of the 27th pick [[Jordan Crawford]] and 31st pick [[Tibor Pleiß]]. On July 15, 2010, he signed a multi-year deal with the Nets and subsequently joined them for the 2010 NBA Summer League. On December 9, 2010, James got his first career start against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].

In January 2012, it was announced that James would miss the rest of the [[2011–12 NBA season]] after undergoing surgery to replace the screw that had been inserted in the broken right foot he suffered the [[2010–11 NBA season|previous season]].<ref>[http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2012/01/injuries_keep_coming_for_nets.html Nets announce Damion James will miss the rest of the season]</ref>
 
On September 12, 2012, he signed with the Atlanta Hawks. However, he was later waived by the Hawks on October 27, 2012.

On November 1, 2012, James was acquired by the [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html Full List of 2012 Returning, Affiliate and Local Tryout Players Invited to NBA D-League Training Camps] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218094230/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html |date=December 18, 2015 }}</ref>

On January 13, 2013, he signed a 10-day with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-damion-james-10-day-contract Nets Sign Damion James to 10-Day Contract]</ref> On January 23, 2013, he returned to the Jam.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Damion-James/Summary/2260 Damion James Player Profile – RealGM]</ref>

On February 4, 2013, James was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html 2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022065410/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |date=October 22, 2013 }}</ref>

In July 2013, James joined the Brooklyn Nets for the Orlando Summer League and the Miami Heat for the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 30, 2013, James signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14376 |title=Denver Nuggets add Reginald Becton, Kyle Fogg, Damion James to training camp |access-date=October 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017132520/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14376 |archive-date=October 17, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Nuggets on October 26, 2013.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14665 Denver Nuggets waive Damion James]</ref>

On December 5, 2013, James was reacquired by the Bakersfield Jam.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/bakersfield_acquires_damion_ja_2013_12_05.html Bakersfield Acquires Damion James]</ref> On February 20, 2014, he was traded to the Texas Legends.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_trade_armor_jam_legends_2014_02_20.html Five Former NBA Players Traded in Three-Team Deal] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301184717/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_trade_armor_jam_legends_2014_02_20.html |date=March 1, 2014 }}</ref> On April 3, 2014, he signed a 10-day contract with the San Antonio Spurs.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140403_spurs_sign_damion_james Spurs Sign Damion James to 10-Day Contract]</ref> On April 13, 2014, he signed with the Spurs for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140413_spurs_sign_damion_james_for_remainder_of_season Spurs Sign Damion James for Remainder of Season]</ref> On June 15, 2014, he won his first NBA championship after the Spurs defeated the [[Miami Heat]] 4 games to 1 in the [[2014 NBA Finals]].

In July 2014, James joined the [[Detroit Pistons]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On September 29, 2014, he signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-six-training-camp Wizards Sign Six for Training Camp]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Wizards on October 25, 2014.<ref>[http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2014/10/25/wizards-waive-james-lucas-silas WIZARDS WAIVE JAMES, LUCAS, SILAS]{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On November 3, 2014, he was reacquired by the Texas Legends.<ref>{{cite web |title=Training Camp Roster |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/2014trainingcamproster.html |work=NBA.com |date=November 3, 2014 |access-date=November 8, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106154143/http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/2014trainingcamproster.html |archive-date=November 6, 2014 }}</ref> On February 17, 2015, he terminated his contract with the Legends. The next day, he signed with the [[Alaska Aces (PBA)|Alaska Aces]] as an import for the [[2015 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/alaska-taps-experienced-damion-james-to-replace-import-dj-covington |title=Alaska taps 'experienced' Damion James to replace import DJ Covington |access-date=February 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150219135604/http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/alaska-taps-experienced-damion-james-to-replace-import-dj-covington |archive-date=February 19, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On August 4, 2015, James signed a one-year deal with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite news|title=DAMION JAMES POUR BOUCLER LA RAQUETTE|url=http://www.msb.fr/index.php/club/44-informations-generales/2843-damion-james-pour-boucler-la-raquette|access-date=December 11, 2015|work=MSB.fr|date=August 4, 2015|language=fr|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222141727/http://www.msb.fr/index.php/club/44-informations-generales/2843-damion-james-pour-boucler-la-raquette|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 20, 2015, he parted ways with Le Mans after appearing in six [[2015–16 LNB Pro A season|league]] games and five [[2015–16 Eurocup Basketball|Eurocup]] games.<ref>{{cite news|title=DAMION JAMES QUITTE LE MSB|url=http://www.msb.fr/index.php/club/44-informations-generales/2960-damion-james-quitte-le-msb|access-date=December 11, 2015|work=MSB.fr|date=November 20, 2015|language=fr|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222153747/http://www.msb.fr/index.php/club/44-informations-generales/2960-damion-james-quitte-le-msb|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 9, 2015, he signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] as an injury replacement for [[Josh Childress]].<ref>{{cite news|title=KINGS SIGN DAMION JAMES AS INJURY REPLACEMENT|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/kings-sign-damion-james-as-injury-replacement/|access-date=December 9, 2015|work=SydneyKings.com|date=December 9, 2015|archive-date=December 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151211175831/http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/kings-sign-damion-james-as-injury-replacement/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on December 29 following the return of Childress. In five games for the Kings, James averaged 7.0 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|last=Decent|first=Tom|title=Josh Childress to return for Sydney Kings as Damion James taken off roster|url=http://www.theage.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-to-return-for-sydney-kings-as-damion-james-taken-off-roster-20151229-glwbuj.html|access-date=December 29, 2015|work=TheAge.com.au|date=December 29, 2015}}</ref> On January 26, 2016, he signed with the [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of Puerto Rico for the 2016 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/189101/damion-james-signs-with-cangrejeros-de-santurce.html Damion James signs with Cangrejeros de Santurce]</ref>

In August 2016, James signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto%20Rico/news/459197/Guaros-ink-Damion-James,-ex-Santurce|title=Guaros ink Damion James, ex Santurce|publisher=Latinbasket.com|date=August 7, 2016|access-date=September 16, 2016}}</ref>

On November 4, 2017, James signed with the Israeli team [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] for the 2017–18 season, joining his former teammate [[Mike Rosario]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sport5.co.il/articles.aspx?FolderID=274&docID=256417&lang=HE|title=סגל הזרים הושלם: דמיון ג'יימס חתם באילת|publisher=Sport5.co.il|date=November 4, 2017|access-date=November 4, 2017|language=he}}</ref> However, on December 13, 2017, he was released by Eilat after appearing in four games.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.one.co.il/Article/17-18/2,620,6753,0/303513.html|title=מוקדם מהצפוי: אילת שחררה את דמיון ג'יימס|publisher=one.co.il|date=December 13, 2017|access-date=December 13, 2017|language=he}}</ref> On December 31, he signed with [[Capitanes de Arecibo]] of Puerto Rico.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://canchalatina.com/2017/12/31/damion-james-y-cinco-jugadores-nacionales-reforzaran-a-capitanes-de-arecibo-en-la-liga-de-las-americas/|title=DAMION JAMES Y CUATRO JUGADORES NACIONALES REFORZARÁN A CAPITANES DE ARECIBO EN LA LIGA DE LAS AMÉRICAS|work=CanchaLatina.com|date=December 31, 2017|access-date=May 5, 2018|language=es}}</ref>

On May 17, 2018, James signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of Puerto Rico after a two-game stint with [[Cariduros de Fajardo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/damionjamesreemplazaraarickyledoenbayamon-2422914/|title=Damion James reemplazará a Ricky Ledo en Bayamón|work=ElNuevoDia.com|date=May 17, 2018|access-date=May 19, 2018|language=es}}</ref>
